blocks.content:
• President – Constitutional head
• Prime Minister – Real executive
• Vice President – Chairman of Rajya Sabha
• Article 72 – Pardoning power
• Article 74 – Council to aid President
• Electoral college excludes nominated members
• Minimum age for President – 35 years

items: Article 72 (Pardoning power) and Article 74 (Council to aid President) are frequently matched in constitutional matching questions.
Nominated members do NOT participate in the Presidential election (Electoral College).
The minimum age qualification for the President is 35 years.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The President acts as the Constitutional head of India, whereas the Prime Minister is the real executive.
The Vice President serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Article 72 defines the President's pardoning power, while Article 74 mandates a Council of Ministers to aid the President.
Nominated members of Parliament are excluded from the Presidential Electoral College.
A minimum age of 35 years is required to become the President of India.
